issues.description: The exercise requires a static method on SealSaloon that computes a Meal's total price, but the method name is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement and UML specify calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int (problem_statement.md). In the solution SealSaloon the static method is implemented as public static int computeMealCost(Meal meal) (src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java). The template Main calls shop.computeMealCost(...) (TEMPLATE_REPOSITORY/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java) while the solution Main calls shop.calculateTotalPrice(...) (SOLUTION_REPOSITORY/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java). This naming mismatch (calculateTotalPrice vs computeMealCost) will confuse students about which method to implement and may cause compilation errors when example code or tests expect the other name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across the problem statement, template/example code, and implementation. Options: (1) Rename the solution's method computeMealCost to calculateTotalPrice with signature public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal) and update all references; (2) Add a public static wrapper calculateTotalPrice(Meal) in SealSaloon that delegates to computeMealCost; or (3) Change the problem statement/UML to require computeMealCost if that name is intended. Ensure the chosen name and signature (static, parameter Meal, return int) are used consistently in Main, the tests, and the documentation.
